sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
The clicks on TC, MC, BC only changed the tiles (lit up), and the gameplay objects didn't move. The pattern is complete (all 3 lit up), but no movement occurred. Wait — did the pattern actually complete? The tile lit-up state: let me check whether the tile is currently N (lit). In the snapshot, the M block on the panel is shown, but the tile isn't shown. Let me check the tile's color and whether the pattern was "completed" (in level 2, completion caused a reset + movement).
Actually, in level 2, when the 3rd tile was lit, the payload moved AND the tile reset. Here, after BC, the objects didn't change. Maybe the completion effect is different: perhaps the pink block needs to be moved via arrow keys, and the pattern is for something else. Or, the pattern's target might not be the center column — the white tiles might just be the initial state, and the actual target is indicated by the 2nd panel (the vertical stack of 3 M's).
Wait, in level 2 the white tiles were exactly the target (TL, TC, MC), and the hint panel showed the same 3 blocks. Here, the white tiles are TC, MC, BC (center column), and the 2nd panel shows a vertical stack of 3 M's — consistent: the target pattern is the center column.
I lit up all 3. Did anything happen? The objects didn't move. Hmm, but maybe the completion effect requires the tiles to be lit in a specific order, or maybe the effect is that the pink block becomes "movable" (released) via arrow keys.
Let me check the current tile state and test the arrow keys (LEFT should move the pink block toward the port/blob).

sections.label: TOOL CALL: python
sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
L=current_frame.ascii.split('\n')
print("tiles:", [(r,c,L[r][c]) for r in (50,55,60) for c in (25,30,35) if L[r][c] in 'WN'])
action(['LEFT'])
r0=last_action_result
print("LEFT: changed", r0.get('board_changed'), "lvl", r0.get('level_completed'), "done", r0.get('done'))
seg=current_frame.segmentation
for n in seg['nodes']:
    if n['color'] in 'MrbS':
        b=n['boundary']; rs=[p[0] for p in b]; cs=[p[1] for p in b]
        print(n['color'], min(rs), max(rs), min(cs), max(cs), n['pixels'])
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
